anomalies.observed: U34 (SN74LVC1G07, open-drain buffer) has its input A (pin2) tied directly to +3V3 and its output Y (pin4) on /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV, while R58 pulls that same net to GND (R58.1=GND, R58.2=/LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV). An open-drain buffer with A=high can only go high-Z, so with a pull-down resistor the net is permanently 0 V. That net is the gate of the WS2812 low-side ground switch Q10 and the OE of the WS2812 level-shifter U7 (TXS0101).
anomalies.expected: The /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV enable must be able to go high to turn on Q10 (connecting the WS2812 VSS to GND) and to enable U7, so the spec-stated addressable status LEDs can operate. Either R58 should be a pull-up to a supply and U34's input tied low (so /LED_EN can pull the net down to disable), or the net should be sourced by an active driver.
anomalies.impact: All seven WS2812B status LEDs are permanently unpowered/disabled (Q10 off leaves their VSS floating and U7 OE low blocks the data line), so the board's addressable status-LED feature described in the spec does not work.

anomalies.observed: The 2-bit CAN termination DIP switch SW6 is wired so that switch 1 (pins1-2) joins R34.2 (/CAN0_N side) to R35.2 (/CAN1_N side), and switch 2 (pins3-4) joins /CAN1_P (pin3) directly to /CAN0_P (pin4). Neither switch ever places a 120R resistor across its own CAN pair, and closing switch 2 shorts the high lines of the two separate buses together.
anomalies.expected: Each DIP-switch pole should bridge one termination resistor across its own bus (R34 between /CAN0_N and /CAN0_P, R35 between /CAN1_N and /CAN1_P). The spec describes two isolated/separate CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1); a termination switch must not merge them.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515

anomalies.impact: The CAN termination option is non-functional, and actuating the switch shorts CAN0_H to CAN1_H, coupling the two buses that the spec says are separate.

anomalies.observed: The second element of the dual e-stop/status LED D30 has its anode A2 (pin4) on ESTOP_OUT and its cathode K2 (pin2) returned through R60, but R60's other end (pin2) is also on ESTOP_OUT. So D30 and R60 form a closed loop from ESTOP_OUT back to ESTOP_OUT with no return to GND or to a supply.
anomalies.expected: For the e-stop indicator element to light, its cathode resistor must return to GND (or the anode to the LED power net) so a voltage appears across the LED; the reference-style first element (D30 A1/K1 with R59 to GND) shows the intended pattern.
anomalies.impact: The red e-stop status LED in D30 never lights, removing the visual e-stop indication on the board.

parsed.summary: The spec-named components (crystals, TVS, LTC4412, buffers, MCP2515, ISL54222, GLOBAL_EN/SW1) all match the netlist, but several undocumented connections deviate from sound design and from the spec's stated features: the WS2812 enable/power net /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV is permanently held low (U34 open-drain with A tied high plus R58 pull-down), disabling all addressable status LEDs; the CAN termination DIP switch SW6 is mis-wired so it cannot terminate either bus and instead shorts CAN0_P to CAN1_P when closed; and the D30 e-stop LED's cathode resistor R60 returns to the LED's own anode net rather than GND, leaving that indicator dead.

response.reasoning:
We need to review the design files for the AcornRobotElectronics board (cm4_robot_board motherboard) against the design specification. The netlist is the authoritative connectivity. We need to look for anomalies: deviations from intended design that would make board behave differently.

Let me work through systematically.

First, understand the spec: CM4 motherboard, RS-485 discrepancy noted (README says RS-485 but netlist shows CAN - this is documented as observed, not anomaly). CAN controllers U8, U9 MCP2515 with 16MHz crystals Y1, Y2. Isolated CAN transceivers U10, U11 (ISO1050DUB / CA-IS3050G). E-stop buffers U15, U22, U35, U36 SN74LVC1G07. U6 LTC4412 ideal diode. Module1 pin 99 Global_EN tied to SW1 pin 2. D9, D10 CDSOT23-SM712 TVS on CAN0/CAN1. U5 ISL54222AIUZ analog switch. WS2812B LEDs D5-D7, D18-D21.

Let me check the crystal values: Y1 and Y2 are 16MHz per spec (corrected). Netlist shows Y1 value "16MHz", Y2 value "16MHz". Good.

Now let's check the CAN crystal nets. U8 OSC1 pin 8, OSC2 pin 7. U9 OSC1 pin 8, OSC2 pin 7.

Net 150 "Net-(U8-OSC1)": C10 pin1, U8 pin8, Y2 pin1.
Net 151 "Net-(U8-OSC2)": C8 pin1, U8 pin7, Y2 pin3.
Net 153 "Net-(U9-OSC1)": C7 pin1, U9 pin8, Y1 pin1.
Net 154 "Net-(U9-OSC2)": C4 pin1, U9 pin7, Y1 pin3.

So Y2 is for U8, Y1 for U9. Both 16MHz. Good.

Now check the CAN transceiver connections. U10 and U11 are isolated CAN transceivers (ISO1050DUB). Pins: 1 VCC1, 2 RXD, 3 TXD, 4 GND1, 5 GND2, 6 CANL, 7 CANH, 8 VCC2.

Net 156 "Net-(U10-RXD)": U10 pin2 RXD, U9 pin2 RXCAN.
Net 157 "Net-(U10-TXD)": U10 pin3 TXD, U9 pin1 TXCAN.
Net 174 "RXLED": U11 pin2 RXD, U19 pin2 A, U8 pin2 RXCAN.
Net 196 "TXLED": U11 pin3 TXD, U18 pin2 A, U8 pin1 TXCAN.

Wait, this is interesting. U8 (MCP2515) TXCAN/RXCAN are connected to U11's TXD/RXD. U9's TXCAN/RXCAN connected to U10's TXD/RXD.

But the spec says U11 and companion drive CAN buses. Let's look at the CAN bus nets.

Net 5 "/CAN0_N": D10 pin1, J13 pin8, J2 pin8, R34 pin1, U11 pin6 CANL.
Net 6 "/CAN0_P": D10 pin2, J13 pin5, J2 pin5, SW6 pin4, U11 pin7 CANH.
Net 7 "/CAN1_N": D9 pin1, J13 pin3, J2 pin3, R35 pin1, U10 pin6 CANL.
Net 8 "/CAN1_P": D9 pin2, J13 pin2, J2 pin2, SW6 pin3, U10 pin7 CANH.

So U11 drives CAN0, U10 drives CAN1. And U11's RXD/TXD connect to U8's RXCAN/TXCAN. U10's RXD/TXD connect to U9's RXCAN/TXCAN. That's consistent: U8->U11->CAN0, U9->U10->CAN1. Good.

Now the LED buffers: spec says U18, U19 (SN74LVC1G07) driving TXLED/RXLED nets from U8 TXCAN/RXCAN. Indeed U18 pin2 A connected to TXLED net which also has U8 pin1 TXCAN and U11 pin3 TXD. U19 pin2 A connected to RXLED net which has U8 pin2 RXCAN and U11 pin2 RXD. Good.

Now let's look at the e-stop sink buffers. Spec: U15, U22, U35, U36 SN74LVC1G07 wired as /OE gates on ESTOP_SINK1/ESTOP_SINK2/ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL feeding ESTOP_OUT.

SN74LVC1G07 pinout (libpart acorn-motherboard): pin1 /OE, pin2 A, pin3 GND, pin4 Y, pin5 VCC.

Let's check each:
U22: pin1 /OE = ESTOP_SINK1 (net68), pin2 A = GND (net80 has U22 pin2 A), pin4 Y = Net-(U15-A) (net164), pin5 VCC = +3V3.
U15: pin1 /OE = ESTOP_SINK2 (net69), pin2 A = Net-(U15-A) (net164), pin4 Y = Net-(U15-Y) (net165), pin5 VCC = +3V3.
U35: pin1 /OE = ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL (net70), pin2 A = Net-(U15-Y) (net165), pin4 Y = /ESTOP_SINK_ALL (net17), pin5 VCC = +3V3.
U36: pin1 /OE = /ESTOP_SINK_ALL (net17), pin2 A = ESTOP (net66, GPIO6), pin4 Y = ESTOP_OUT (net67), pin5 VCC = +3V3.

Hmm, this is a chain of buffers. The /OE pins are connected to the ESTOP_SINK nets (which are the e-stop loop inputs), and the A inputs are tied in a chain. This is the "wired as /OE-controlled sinks" described. The spec says "single non-inverting buffers wired as /OE-controlled sinks". OK.

Now check U36 pin2 A = ESTOP net (GPIO6). That's the local e-stop input from CM4. Fine.

Now let's look at the power rails and check for shorts.

+3V3 net (code1): includes U20 pin2 VO (LDO output), Module1 pin78 GPIO_VREF, lots of caps, buffers VCC, etc. Also includes U34 pin2 A and U34 pin5 VCC both on +3V3? Let's check: net1 has U34 pin2 A and U34 pin5 VCC. U34 is SN74LVC1G07. Pin2 A tied to +3V3 (VCC). That means the input A is tied high. Pin1 /OE = /LED_EN, pin4 Y = /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV. So U34 is a buffer with input tied high, output drives LED power enable. That's fine - it's used as a gated driver (OE controlled). OK.

Also net1 includes U7 pin1 VCCA (TXS0101 level shifter). OK.

Now +5V net (code2): includes U3 pin4 FB (LM2576 feedback), U6 pin6 SENSE (LTC4412 sense), U12 pin4 EN and pin5 VIN, U2 pin5 VCC, U27 pin2 A and pin5 VCC, U29 pin5 VCC, Q1 pin2 S, Q6 pin2 S, Q9 pin2 S, Module1 5V inputs, F1 pin1, F2 pin2, L1 pin2, L2 pin1, etc.

Wait, U27 pin2 A = +5V and U27 pin5 VCC = +5V. U27 is SN74LVC1G07. Pin2 A tied to VCC (high). Pin1 /OE = /LED_EN, pin4 Y = Net-(D2-A) which drives D2 LED. So U27 is a driver with input high, output to LED. OK that's a sink driver for LED. Fine.

U2 pin5 VCC = +5V, pin2 A = RUN_PG (net173), pin1 /OE = GND (net80 has U2 pin1 /OE), pin4 Y = Net-(U2-Y) = SW1 pin1 (net149). Hmm U2 is a buffer with /OE tied to GND (enabled), input A = RUN_PG, output Y = SW1 pin1. And SW1 pin2 = GLOBAL_EN. So SW1 is a tactile switch between U2 output and GLOBAL_EN. Interesting. Actually that's the power enable path. The spec says GLOBAL_EN tied directly to SW1 pin2. Yes net79 GLOBAL_EN has Module1 pin99 and SW1 pin2. And SW1 pin1 goes to U2 Y. So pressing SW1 connects RUN_PG-derived signal to GLOBAL_EN. Hmm, that's a bit odd but it's the design. Not necessarily anomaly.

Wait, but U2's /OE is tied to GND which enables it. U2 VCC = +5V. SN74LVC1G07 is open-drain buffer. Input A = RUN_PG (CM4 pin92 RUN_PG output). Output Y = SW1 pin1. So when RUN_PG high, Y sinks SW1 pin1 to GND? No, open drain: when input high, output is low (sink). When input low, output high-Z. Hmm. This is the e-stop? Not sure. Not our focus.

Let's look at +12V net (code3): C19 pin1, C20 pin1, D11 pin1 K, J12 pin1, J22 pin2, R17 pin2. D11 is MBR0530 Schottky. D11 pin1 K = +12V, pin2 A = Net-(D11-A) which has L2 pin2 and U12 pin1 SW. U12 is TPS61040 LED boost driver. So U12 boost output via D11 to +12V. J12 is a connector pin1 = +12V. J22 is DNP connector pin2 = +12V. OK.

Now check the LTC4412 U6. Pins: 1 VIN, 2 GND, 3 CTL, 4 STAT, 5 GATE, 6 SENSE.
Net206 USBC_VBUS_IN: J3 VBUS pins, Q1 pin3 D, R11 pin1, R64 pin2, U25 pin5 VBUS, U6 pin1 VIN. So U6 VIN = USBC_VBUS_IN. Good.
U6 pin6 SENSE = +5V (net2). Hmm. In LTC4412, SENSE pin connects to the sense side of the MOSFET (the load side / output side of the FET). For ideal diode, the MOSFET is between input and output; SENSE monitors the output side voltage to detect reverse current. Let's think. The P-MOSFET Q1: pin1 G = Net-(Q1-G) = U6 pin5 GATE (net137). pin2 S = +5V (net2). pin3 D = USBC_VBUS_IN (net206). So Q1 source is +5V, drain is USBC_VBUS_IN. The gate driven by U6. U6 VIN = USBC_VBUS_IN (the input side, which is the drain? or source?). Hmm.

Actually for a P-MOS ideal diode, current flows from source to drain (i.e., from +5V side to USBC_VBUS_IN side?) Wait, that's reverse of typical. Let's think about the topology. The USB-C input provides VBUS (USBC_VBUS_IN). That should power the +5V rail. So current flows from USBC_VBUS_IN through the FET to +5V. For a P-MOS, source should be the higher potential side = USBC_VBUS_IN, drain = +5V. But here Q1 source pin2 = +5V and drain pin3 = USBC_VBUS_IN. That's swapped relative to typical ideal diode orientation. Hmm but maybe they're using it as a load switch with the body diode orientation? Actually P-MOS body diode goes from drain to source (anode at source? Let's recall: For a P-MOS, the body diode anode is at source? Hmm. Actually in MOSFET symbol, body diode arrow points from source to drain for N-MOS? Let's recall: For N-channel, body diode anode at source, cathode at drain (conducts source->drain? No). Hmm I'm getting confused.

Let's not overthink; the spec documents the USB diode/ideal diode as a known open issue ("USB diode doesn't work"). So even if topology is questionable, it's a documented limitation, not an anomaly to report. The spec explicitly says this is a documented open/partially-resolved issue. So we should NOT report U6/Q1 orientation.

Now U6 pin3 CTL = /~{VBUS_5V_ENA} (net46) via R64 pull-up to USBC_VBUS_IN and D31 pin2 A. U6 pin4 STAT = unconnected (net316). U6 pin2 GND = GND. OK.

Now let's look at the CAN termination and SW6. SW6 is SW_DIP_x02 (2-bit DIP switch). Pins: net6 /CAN0_P has SW6 pin4. net8 /CAN1_P has SW6 pin3. net145 Net-(R34-Pad2) has SW6 pin1 and R34 pin2. net146 Net-(R35-Pad2) has SW6 pin2 and R35 pin2. R34 pin1 = /CAN0_N, R35 pin1 = /CAN1_N. So R34 (120R) is termination for CAN0, switched via SW6 bit1 (pins1-2) between /CAN0_N and /CAN0_P. Similarly R35 for CAN1 via SW6 pins3-4. That's standard CAN termination switch. Good.

Now let's check the TVS D9, D10. D9 = CDSOT23-SM712 on CAN1: pin1 input = /CAN1_N, pin2 input = /CAN1_P, pin3 output = GND. Good. D10 on CAN0: pin1 = /CAN0_N, pin2 = /CAN0_P, pin3 = GND. Good.

Now check U5 and U24 (ISL54222AIUZ analog switches). U5 pins: 1 SEL, 2 HSD1+, 3 HSD2+, 4 D+, 5 GND, 6 D-, 7 HSD2-, 8 HSD1-, 9 *OE, 10 VDD.
Net208 USB_OTG: Module1 pin101 USB_OTG_ID, R11 pin2, R9 pin1, U5 pin1 SEL. OK SEL tied to OTG ID.
Net207 USB_N: Module1 pin103 USB2_N, U5 pin6 D-.
Net209 USB_P: Module1 pin105 USB2_P, U5 pin4 D+.
Net198 USBAP_D_N: U26 pin6 I/O1, U5 pin8 HSD1-.
Net199 USBAP_D_P: U26 pin4 I/O2, U5 pin2 HSD1+.
Net212 USB_SW_D+: JP7 pin1 A, U24 pin2 HSD1+, U5 pin3 HSD2+.
Net213 USB_SW_D-: JP6 pin1 A, U24 pin8 HSD1-, U5 pin7 HSD2-.
U5 pin5 GND = GND (net80). U5 pin9 *OE = GND (net80). U5 pin10 VDD = +3V3. OK.

U24 pins: 1 SEL = SER_SELECT (net187), 2 HSD1+ = USB_SW_D+, 3 HSD2+ = USB_SERIAL_D+ (net210), 4 D+ = USBCP_D_P (net203), 5 GND = GND, 6 D- = USBCP_D_N (net202), 7 HSD2- = USB_SERIAL_D- (net211), 8 HSD1- = USB_SW_D-, 9 *OE = GND (net80), 10 VDD = +3V3. OK.

Now check U25, U26 USBLC6-2P6 ESD. U25 pins: 1 I/O1 = USBCP_D_P, 2 GND = GND, 3 I/O2 = USBCP_D_N, 4 I/O2 = USBC_D_N (net204), 5 VBUS = USBC_VBUS_IN, 6 I/O1 = USBC_D_P (net205). Hmm wait U25 pin3 I/O2 = USBCP_D_N and pin4 I/O2 = USBC_D_N. The libpart USBLC6-2P6 has pins 1 I/O1, 2 GND, 3 I/O2, 4 I/O2, 5 VBUS, 6 I/O1. So pins 3 and 4 are both I/O2 (the two ends of one data line ESD), pins 1 and 6 both I/O1. So U25: I/O1 (pin1) = USBCP_D_P, I/O1 (pin6) = USBC_D_P; I/O2 (pin3) = USBCP_D_N, I/O2 (pin4) = USBC_D_N; VBUS pin5 = USBC_VBUS_IN. Good, that's proper ESD across the switch to USB-C connector.

U26: pin1 I/O1 = USBA_D_N (net200), pin2 GND = GND, pin3 I/O2 = USBA_D_P (net201), pin4 I/O2 = USBAP_D_P (net199), pin5 VBUS = /5V_FUSED (net4), pin6 I/O1 = USBAP_D_N (net198). Hmm. U26 protects the USB-A host connector J7. J7 pin2 D- = USBA_D_N, pin3 D+ = USBA_D_P. And U5 HSD1 = USBAP_D_P/N which is the other side of U5 switch going to... wait U5 HSD1+ = USBAP_D_P (U26 pin4), HSD1- = USBAP_D_N (U26 pin6). And U5 D+/D- = USB2_P/N (CM4). And U5 HSD2+/- = USB_SW_D+/- which go to U24 HSD1 and JP7/JP6. Hmm this is a USB routing mess but it's the analog switch matrix for routing CM4 USB vs serial USB to connectors. Probably intended. Not focusing.

Now, important: check the spec's claim about RS-485 vs CAN. The spec already reports this discrepancy as observed, not anomaly. So we don't report.

Now let's look for actual anomalies. The task: design files may be correct. We need to find deviations. Let's look carefully at component values and footprints and net assignments.

Let's check the crystals Y3, Y4 = 14.7456MHz for U13/U14 SC16IS752 UART. That's fine (14.7456 is standard for UART baud). Load caps C21-C24 = 22pF. Good.

Now check U8/U9 reset pullups: R5, R6 = 10K to SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V. Good.

Now check the WS2812 chain. D5 DIN = U7 pin4 B (net106). D5 DOUT = D6 DIN (net107). D6 DOUT = D7 DIN (net108). D7 DOUT = D18 DIN (net117). D18 DOUT = D19 DIN (net118). D19 DOUT = D20 DIN (net120). D20 DOUT = D21 DIN (net121). D21 DOUT = J21 pin2 (net122). All VDD = 5V_switched, VSS = Net-(D18-VSS) (net119) which includes Q10 pin3 D. Good. D5-D7, D18-D21 = 7 WS2812B. Spec says D5-D7, D18-D21 (that's 7). Good.

Let me work through systematically.

CAN controllers U8, U9 MCP2515 with 16MHz crystals Y1, Y2. Isolated CAN transceivers U10, U11 (ISO1050DUB / CA-IS3050G). E-stop buffers U15, U22, U35, U36 SN74LVC1G07. U6 LTC4412 ideal diode. Module1 pin 99 Global_EN tied to SW1 pin 2. D9, D10 CDSOT23-SM712 TVS on CAN0/CAN1. U5 ISL54222AIUZ analog switch. WS2812B LEDs D5-D7, D18-D21.

Let me check the crystal values: Y1 and Y2 are 16MHz per spec (corrected). Netlist shows Y1 value "16MHz", Y2 value "16MHz". Good.

Now let's check the CAN crystal nets. U8 OSC1 pin 8, OSC2 pin 7. U9 OSC1 pin 8, OSC2 pin 7.

Net 150 "Net-(U8-OSC1)": C10 pin1, U8 pin8, Y2 pin1.
Net 151 "Net-(U8-OSC2)": C8 pin1, U8 pin7, Y2 pin3.
Net 153 "Net-(U9-OSC1)": C7 pin1, U9 pin8, Y1 pin1.
Net 154 "Net-(U9-OSC2)": C4 pin1, U9 pin7, Y1 pin3.

So Y2 is for U8, Y1 for U9. Both 16MHz. Good.

Now check the CAN transceiver connections. U10 and U11 are isolated CAN transceivers (ISO1050DUB). Pins: 1 VCC1, 2 RXD, 3 TXD, 4 GND1, 5 GND2, 6 CANL, 7 CANH, 8 VCC2.

Net 156 "Net-(U10-RXD)": U10 pin2 RXD, U9 pin2 RXCAN.
Net 157 "Net-(U10-TXD)": U10 pin3 TXD, U9 pin1 TXCAN.
Net 174 "RXLED": U11 pin2 RXD, U19 pin2 A, U8 pin2 RXCAN.
Net 196 "TXLED": U11 pin3 TXD, U18 pin2 A, U8 pin1 TXCAN.

Net 5 "/CAN0_N": D10 pin1, J13 pin8, J2 pin8, R34 pin1, U11 pin6 CANL.
Net 6 "/CAN0_P": D10 pin2, J13 pin5, J2 pin5, SW6 pin4, U11 pin7 CANH.

SW_DIP_x02 libpart pins 1,2,3,4. The switch symbol: typically pin1-pin2 = switch1, pin3-pin4 = switch2.

So switch1 connects SW6 pin1 (=R34 pin2) and SW6 pin2 (=R35 pin2). Switch2 connects SW6 pin3 (= /CAN1_P) and SW6 pin4 (= /CAN0_P).

Thus, closing switch1 shorts R34 pin2 to R35 pin2 (i.e., the two termination resistors' "P-side" ends get tied together, but neither is connected to a CAN_P line). Closing switch2 shorts /CAN1_P to /CAN0_P directly! That's a short between the two CAN bus high lines. And termination is never achieved because R34's P-side (pin2) is not connected to /CAN0_P; instead /CAN0_P is on the other switch.

So the intended wiring (correct termination switch) would be: switch1 between R34 pin2 and /CAN0_P; switch2 between R35 pin2 and /CAN1_P. In the netlist, /CAN0_P and /CAN1_P are placed on SW6 pin4 and pin3 respectively, while R34 pin2 and R35 pin2 are on pin1 and pin2. So the four pins are assigned as: pin1=R34, pin2=R35, pin3=CAN1_P, pin4=CAN0_P. For correct operation with switch1=1-2 and switch2=3-4, you'd want pin1=R34, pin2=CAN0_P (switch1), pin3=R35, pin4=CAN1_P (switch2). So the CAN_P lines are on the wrong switch pins (swapped between the two switches). This is a clear wiring error that, when the termination switch is used, shorts the two CAN buses' H lines.
